question: Does LoRA fine-tuning NVIDIA Cosmos-Reason2-2B on labelled simulator rollout clips turn it into a reliable pick-and-place success critic, including on an unseen person's demo? (Earlier zero-shot Cosmos critics: v1 always 'success', v2 62/116 vs 76/116 majority baseline.)

splits.train: 640 clips: 4 demos (person 1 notebook/markers/notepad, person 2 box) x 2 arms x {raw, fix stack} x seeds 2000-2039 (309 success)
splits.val: 160 clips, seeds 2040-2049 (76 success); used only to keep the better epoch
splits.test: 220 clips: seeds 2050-2059 of the same demos (160) + the author's unseen demo, seeds 2000-2014 (60); 123 success

labels: simulator task success (metrics.score_episode); the model only sees pixels
method: LoRA r=16 alpha=32 dropout=0.05 on language-model attention+MLP projections; vision frozen; AdamW lr 1e-4; batch 1 x accum 8; 2 epochs; loss on answer tokens only
scoring: clip at 4 fps (<=32 frames, 320x240) + fixed question; label = answer ('success'/'failure') with the higher log-likelihood; identical for zero-shot and fine-tuned
metrics: on the unseen user demo separately
